#!/usr/bin/env bash

#FLUX: -J molden@6.7
#FLUX: -q ind-shared
#FLUX: -N 1
#FLUX: -n 1
#FLUX: -c 16
#FLUX: --mem-per-node=32G
#FLUX: -t 02:00:00
#FLUX: -o molden@6.7.o{id}
# Omitted SLURM --account=use300; Flux does not have a direct equivalent for accounting. This is often site-specific and may not affect performance.
# Omitted SLURM --reservation=rocky8u7_testing; Flux does not have a direct equivalent for reservations.
# Note: SLURM output format %N (nodename) is not directly supported in Flux output patterns.

declare -xr LOCAL_TIME="$(date +'%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%z')"
declare -xir UNIX_TIME="$(date +'%s')"

# Note: Using FLUX_JOB_ID which is the Flux equivalent of SLURM_JOB_ID
declare -xr LOCAL_SCRATCH_DIR="/scratch/${USER}/job_${FLUX_JOB_ID}"
declare -xr TMPDIR="${LOCAL_SCRATCH_DIR}"

declare -xr SYSTEM_NAME='expanse'

declare -xr SPACK_VERSION='0.17.3'
declare -xr SPACK_INSTANCE_NAME='cpu'
declare -xr SPACK_INSTANCE_VERSION='b'
declare -xr SPACK_INSTANCE_DIR="/cm/shared/apps/spack/${SPACK_VERSION}/${SPACK_INSTANCE_NAME}/${SPACK_INSTANCE_VERSION}"

# Note: Flux does not provide a standard environment variable for the job script path.
# Using $(readlink -f "$0") as a best-effort replacement for the scontrol command.
declare -xr FLUX_JOB_SCRIPT="$(readlink -f "$0")"
declare -xr FLUX_JOB_MD5SUM="$(md5sum ${FLUX_JOB_SCRIPT})"

# Note: Changed scheduler name to 'flux'
declare -xr SCHEDULER_MODULE='flux'

# Note: Using FLUX_JOB_ID and FLUX_JOB_DEPENDENCIES which are Flux equivalents
# of SLURM_JOB_ID and SLURM_JOB_DEPENDENCY.
echo "${UNIX_TIME} ${FLUX_JOB_ID} ${FLUX_JOB_MD5SUM} ${FLUX_JOB_DEPENDENCIES}" 
echo ""

cat "${FLUX_JOB_SCRIPT}"

module purge
module load "${SCHEDULER_MODULE}"
module list
. "${SPACK_INSTANCE_DIR}/share/spack/setup-env.sh"

declare -xr SPACK_PACKAGE='molden@6.7'
declare -xr SPACK_COMPILER='gcc@10.2.0'
declare -xr SPACK_VARIANTS=''
declare -xr SPACK_DEPENDENCIES="^meson@0.60.0/$(spack find --format '{hash:7}' meson@0.60.0 % ${SPACK_COMPILER})"
declare -xr SPACK_SPEC="${SPACK_PACKAGE} % ${SPACK_COMPILER} ${SPACK_VARIANTS} ${SPACK_DEPENDENCIES}"

printenv

spack config get compilers  
spack config get config  
spack config get mirrors
spack config get modules
spack config get packages
spack config get repos
spack config get upstreams

time -p spack spec --long --namespaces --types "${SPACK_SPEC}"
if [[ "${?}" -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo 'ERROR: spack concretization failed.'
  exit 1
fi

# Note: Using FLUX_TASK_CPUS which is the Flux equivalent of SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK
time -p spack install --jobs "${FLUX_TASK_CPUS}" --fail-fast --yes-to-all "${SPACK_SPEC}"
if [[ "${?}" -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo 'ERROR: spack install failed.'
  exit 1
fi

#spack module lmod refresh --delete-tree -y

# Note: Converted sbatch dependency submission to flux submit
flux submit --depend="after,ok,${FLUX_JOB_ID}" 'py-ase@3.21.1.sh'

sleep 30

reasons: The resource directive '--mem-per-node=32G' is invalid. Flux does not have a direct '--mem-per-node' option like SLURM. Memory should be requested using other available options, such as '--mem-per-cpu', or rely on queue defaults.
issues: The 'SPACK_DEPENDENCIES' variable is constructed at submission time by executing 'spack find'. This could lead to errors if the Spack environment within the job differs from the submission environment, potentially causing the package hash to mismatch.
The script uses 'readlink -f "$0"' to determine its own path. While generally effective, this can be unreliable depending on how the job script is invoked by the scheduler's internals.

This means it will be evaluated in the submission environment where `FLUX_JOB_ID` is not yet defined, leading to an incorrect directory path like '/scratch/user/job_'. This logic should be moved to a point after the script has begun execution within the Flux job allocation.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#SBATCH --job-name=molden@6.7
#SBATCH --account=use300
#SBATCH --reservation=rocky8u7_testing
#SBATCH --partition=ind-shared
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=16
#SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --output=%x.o%j.%N

declare -xr LOCAL_TIME="$(date +'%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%z')"
declare -xir UNIX_TIME="$(date +'%s')"

declare -xr LOCAL_SCRATCH_DIR="/scratch/${USER}/job_${SLURM_JOB_ID}"
declare -xr TMPDIR="${LOCAL_SCRATCH_DIR}"

declare -xr SYSTEM_NAME='expanse'

declare -xr SPACK_VERSION='0.17.3'
declare -xr SPACK_INSTANCE_NAME='cpu'
declare -xr SPACK_INSTANCE_VERSION='b'
declare -xr SPACK_INSTANCE_DIR="/cm/shared/apps/spack/${SPACK_VERSION}/${SPACK_INSTANCE_NAME}/${SPACK_INSTANCE_VERSION}"

declare -xr SLURM_JOB_SCRIPT="$(scontrol show job ${SLURM_JOB_ID} | awk -F= '/Command=/{print $2}')"
declare -xr SLURM_JOB_MD5SUM="$(md5sum ${SLURM_JOB_SCRIPT})"

declare -xr SCHEDULER_MODULE='slurm'

echo "${UNIX_TIME} ${SLURM_JOB_ID} ${SLURM_JOB_MD5SUM} ${SLURM_JOB_DEPENDENCY}" 
echo ""

cat "${SLURM_JOB_SCRIPT}"

module purge
module load "${SCHEDULER_MODULE}"
module list
. "${SPACK_INSTANCE_DIR}/share/spack/setup-env.sh"

declare -xr SPACK_PACKAGE='molden@6.7'
declare -xr SPACK_COMPILER='gcc@10.2.0'
declare -xr SPACK_VARIANTS=''
declare -xr SPACK_DEPENDENCIES="^meson@0.60.0/$(spack find --format '{hash:7}' meson@0.60.0 % ${SPACK_COMPILER})"
declare -xr SPACK_SPEC="${SPACK_PACKAGE} % ${SPACK_COMPILER} ${SPACK_VARIANTS} ${SPACK_DEPENDENCIES}"

printenv

spack config get compilers  
spack config get config  
spack config get mirrors
spack config get modules
spack config get packages
spack config get repos
spack config get upstreams

time -p spack spec --long --namespaces --types "${SPACK_SPEC}"
if [[ "${?}" -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo 'ERROR: spack concretization failed.'
  exit 1
fi

time -p spack install --jobs "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" --fail-fast --yes-to-all "${SPACK_SPEC}"
if [[ "${?}" -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo 'ERROR: spack install failed.'
  exit 1
fi

#spack module lmod refresh --delete-tree -y

sbatch --dependency="afterok:${SLURM_JOB_ID}" 'py-ase@3.21.1.sh'

sleep 30
